record.hypothesis: Across all four datasets, test a bounded causal popularity-change input feature: scale each existing history embedding by 1+0.1*tanh(log1p(count(previous_item))-log1p(count(current_item))), using category training counts only. Give the first real item scale 1 and keep padding zero. Relative popularity changes may signal interest shifts more effectively than the previously tested absolute-frequency scaling. Preserve embedding parameters, GRU topology, readout, scoring, loss and optimizer; checkpoint counts and reproduce the feature in inference.

+        input_scale = (1.0 + 0.1 * change) * seq.ne(0).to(log_counts.dtype)
+        emb = self.dropout(self.item_emb(seq) * input_scale.unsqueeze(-1))

category_rationales.rationale: Test bounded causal popularity-change features across all four categories using training interaction counts only. Scale history embeddings by 1+0.1*tanh(log1p(previous count)-log1p(current count)); keep the first real item's scale at 1 and padding zero. Preserve learned embeddings, GRU topology, readout, loss and optimizer. Checkpoint the counts in a registered buffer; the generated predictor imports this same model class and restores the buffer through its existing state_dict loader.
